column1: # Cortex sync manifest — how each path propagates from rnc to downstream projects.
#   OVERWRITE  — never edited downstream; the transform writes straight to the project
#                worktree (the AI-tooling layer: rules, commands, hooks, cortex knowledge).
#   MERGE      — editable downstream; the transform lands on the `rnc-upstream` vendor
#                branch and git 3-way-merges into main (all sub-project code + tests + config).
#   LOCAL      — the project owns it; sync NEVER touches it (identity, brand, roster).
#   SKIP       — never synced at all (sync metadata, local-only files).
#   RETIRED    — a path rnc renamed or removed. Never tracked here; downstream the sync reports
#                every file that still matches, and deletes them with --prune-retired.
# Matching: FIRST MATCH WINS — list specific LOCAL/SKIP/OVERWRITE exceptions ABOVE the broad
# catch-alls. A path matches if it equals the entry, the entry ends with '/' and is a path
# prefix, or the entry contains '*' (fnmatch glob; '*' spans '/'). Every tracked file MUST
# resolve to a mode — there is NO implicit default; the final `*` catch-all guarantees it.
# Classification scans git-tracked files only — build artifacts (node_modules/, vendor/,
# dist/, playwright-report/, test-results/) are gitignored and never seen.
# ---- RETIRED: renamed or removed upstream; must not live on downstream ----
# The command generation before the `battoni-` prefix. Projects bootstrapped before the rename kept
# both generations, because the sync writes what rnc has and never deletes what it dropped.
# Laravel Boost's generated copies of the root arcus-* skills: two versions of one skill, and the
# copy loaded only in a session opened inside api.rnc/. boost.json no longer targets claude_code.
# rnc's own documentation portal (built from the docs-portal skill). It documents
# THIS monorepo, so it must never propagate. manifest.tsv is itself specialized on sync,
# so this becomes `SKIP docs.<project>/` downstream — protecting each project's own docs.
# rnc's OWN public landing site (the battoni.dev brand instance + landing-page reference
# template). It is brand content for THIS repo — it must never propagate verbatim into a client
# project (the rnc->project word-map does not rewrite the literal `battoni.dev` path). Each
# project bootstraps its own `public.<project>`. Specialized on sync to `SKIP public.<project>/`.
# ---- LOCAL: project identity / brand / roster — never overwritten ----
# Core/local extension points: every *.local.* file (routes.local.ts, navItems.local.ts,
# api.local.php, LocalSeeder.php via *.local naming, locales/local/*) is the project-owned
# half of a synced core file. Projects register their feature wiring here so a sync can NEVER
# revert it — the structural fix for the silent-revert class of bug. rnc ships these as
# empty stubs (MERGE would defeat the purpose, so they are LOCAL even in rnc).
# Feature folders (.claude/feature-flow.md): the intent, spec, plan and state of THIS project's work.
# The project's brand chain at the repo root, written by the `battoni-new-brand` skill (the
# survey, SYSTEM.md, design-system/). It is identity: a `MERGE *` keeps it safe only while
# rnc ships no `brand/` of its own, and the first one it shipped would merge into every child.
# Dependency lock files: each project regenerates its own (npm/composer install) and
# pins its own versions — rnc must never overwrite or merge them.
# Deploy: the workflow and the script that publishes an API to a server.
# LOCAL and it is a SAFETY rule, not tidiness. A deploy names a host, a path and an SSH
# account that belong to exactly one project — and rnc's script runs
# `migrate:fresh --seed`, which is correct for a bootstrap that keeps no data and would
# DESTROY the database of a child that has shipped. lifeshifter has had real user data
# since 2026-08-31. As MERGE this file would arrive there as a conflict somebody resolves
# at 6pm, and the resolution would be a dropped production database.
# Each project writes its own, from its own premises. What travels is the shape, by
# Retired (2026-11-04): "the session command lists THIS repo's sub-projects, so each project owns
# its copy" — LOCAL froze every child's copy (four still said "read all five files" with nine
# rules shipped), and `/battoni-start-session <id>`, the build step of the feature flow, could
# never reach them. The command now reads the sub-projects from the root CLAUDE.md's table,
# which IS local, and travels with the rest of .claude/ as OVERWRITE.
# A project's PLANS are the project's. `cortex/` is OVERWRITE, which is right for the knowledge
# the bootstrap owns and catastrophic for a phase tracker: largatudoevai's README lists nine real
# phases and their PRs, and a sync would replace it with the empty template shipped here. The
# tracker's SHAPE travels — it is written down in the file — but its contents never do.
# Visual identity / brand — each project keeps its own; rnc must NEVER overwrite it.
# colors.css is the declared "brand contract"; logo + favicons + the page title are identity.
# Brand-mark atoms + the brand style-guide view ARE identity (the mark, pattern, signature,
# and showcase). Project-owned so a client's brand never reverts to rnc's — and rnc's
# brand never ships into a client (keeps --brand-audit clean).
# ---- OVERWRITE: AI-tooling layer — safe to overwrite (not edited downstream) ----
# ---- MERGE: everything else — all sub-project code, tests, config, root tooling ----
# Covers app.rnc, api.rnc, codelumen, liquen, vitrum + Makefile, .github/ (CI), .gitignore,
# .nvmrc, .vscode/, CLAUDE.local.md.example. Conservative by design: MERGE never silently
# overwrites — it surfaces a git conflict only where BOTH sides changed the same lines.
# Retune specific brand/identity files up to LOCAL as churn reveals them.
